question: Find the part with an error: The proposal was not only (A) / cost-effective but also (B) / it was easy to implement. (C)
explanation: Faulty parallelism: 'not only cost-effective but also easy to implement'.

question: Improve the part in capitals: She prefers walking in the morning RATHER THAN to cycle in the evening.
explanation: 'Prefer X to Y' with gerunds.

question: He was reluctant to _____ his opinion lest it should _____ his superiors.
explanation: Fear of offending explains reluctance to voice an opinion.

question: Improve the part in capitals: The two brothers help EACH OTHERS during crises.
explanation: 'Each other' has no plural form.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. The profit and loss statement, by contrast, tracks income and expenditure over a period.
Q. Investors need to read both documents together to judge a firm's health.
R. A balance sheet records what a company owns and what it owes at a given moment.
S. It therefore offers a snapshot rather than a running account of performance.
explanation: R defines, S explains 'therefore', P contrasts, Q concludes.

question: Improve the part in capitals: The CEO, WHO'S decisions were widely criticised, finally resigned.
explanation: Possessive 'whose' is needed, not 'who is'.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. The usual tool is the policy interest rate.
Q. Inflation erodes the purchasing power of money over time.
R. Raising it makes borrowing costlier and thus cools demand.
S. Central banks therefore try to keep it within a target band.
explanation: Problem, response, tool, mechanism.

question: Neither the borrower _____ the guarantors _____ able to repay the loan.
explanation: 'Neither ... nor' with the nearer plural subject takes 'were'.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. The model was soon replicated in many developing countries, including India.
Q. Repayment rates turned out to be remarkably high.
R. Microfinance began as a modest experiment in Bangladesh.
S. Small loans were given to poor women without collateral.
explanation: Origin, method, result, replication.

question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The annual report was VERBOSE and difficult to navigate.
explanation: Verbose means wordy.

question: Improve the part in capitals: HAD I KNOWN about the delay, I would have informed you earlier.
explanation: The inverted third conditional is correct.

question: Improve the part in capitals: I wish I WAS taller.
explanation: Subjunctive after 'wish'.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The defendant's argument was FALLACIOUS.
explanation: A fallacious argument is based on faulty reasoning.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: His SANGUINE outlook persisted despite repeated losses.
explanation: Sanguine means hopeful.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To rest on one's laurels.
options: To be content with past success and make no further effort
explanation: It means relying on earlier achievements.

question: Find the part with an error: Whom do you think (A) / will be appointed as (B) / the next branch head? (C)
explanation: 'Who' is the subject of 'will be appointed'.

question: Improve the part in capitals: Hardly had the bell rung THAN the students dashed out.
explanation: 'Hardly ... when' is the correct pairing.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 2)
options: I have been working here since five years.
She doesn't hardly speak to anyone.
The committee has completed its inquiry.
Between you and I, the plan will fail.
explanation: The collective noun acts as a unit, matching 'its'.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. In the short run, the meltwater may actually increase river flow.
Q. Planners must therefore begin preparing for water scarcity today.
R. Glaciers in the Himalayas are retreating at an alarming pace.
S. Over the long run, however, the supply is bound to shrink.
T. This matters because they feed rivers that sustain hundreds of millions of people.
explanation: Fact, significance, short run, long run, conclusion.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To blow the whistle.
explanation: It means to reveal illicit activity.

question: Find the part with an error: I would have (A) / helped you if you (B) / would have asked me. (C)
explanation: The if-clause of a third conditional takes 'had asked'.

question: Since the evidence was merely _____ , the judge refused to _____ the accused.
explanation: Merely circumstantial evidence is too weak to convict.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. Liberalisation in the 1990s changed the picture dramatically.
Q. Mobile services then spread so quickly that even remote villages gained access.
R. Growth was slow for the next hundred years, as connections remained a luxury.
S. The first telephone exchange in India opened in Calcutta in 1881.
explanation: Chronological order of events.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: She is BRUSHING UP ON her accounting knowledge.
explanation: Brush up on means revise to improve.

question: Find the part with an error: Of the two proposals, (A) / the first is (B) / the most feasible one. (C)
explanation: For two items the comparative 'the more feasible' is needed.

question: The committee (A) / have decided to (B) / postpone it's meeting. (C)
explanation: 'its' (possessive) is correct; 'it's' means 'it is'.

question: Find the part with an error: If the rains (A) / would fail again this year, (B) / farmers will face acute distress. (C)
explanation: 'Would' is not used in an if-clause of a first conditional; use 'fail'.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The auditor's PERFUNCTORY inspection missed several irregularities.
explanation: Perfunctory means done with minimal effort.

question: Find the part with an error: Despite of (A) / repeated warnings from the regulator, (B) / the lender continued to flout the norms. (C)
explanation: 'Despite' is not followed by 'of'; 'in spite of' or 'despite' alone is correct.

question: The bank's profits _____ sharply in the third quarter, _____ analysts' expectations.
explanation: Surge and exceeding expectations are consistent.

question: Find the part with an error: It is high time (A) / the management took (B) / strict action against defaulters. (C)
explanation: 'It is high time' correctly takes the simple past.

question: Improve the part in capitals: She is one of those officers who ALWAYS COMPLETES her work on time.
explanation: 'Who' refers to the plural 'officers'.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The company's CIRCUMSPECT approach to expansion helped it survive the downturn.
explanation: Circumspect means wary of risks.

question: The scheme was launched with great _____ but soon _____ for want of funds.
explanation: Grand launch followed by failure.

question: Improve the part in capitals: The new scheme is more beneficial THAN ANY scheme launched so far.
explanation: Comparison within the same class needs 'other'.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. Consequently, farmers are forced to either replant or switch to less profitable varieties.
Q. A delay of even a fortnight can disturb the sowing calendar of major crops.
R. Such disruptions eventually push up food prices in the cities.
S. Agriculture in India depends heavily on the timely arrival of the monsoon.
explanation: General statement, delay, consequence, then price effect.

question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: He was an OBSTINATE negotiator who rarely yielded.
explanation: Obstinate means stubborn; pliable means yielding.

question: Find the part with an error: One should (A) / always keep their (B) / promises. (C)
explanation: The pronoun must agree with 'one': 'one's promises'.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. A downgrade, in contrast, makes borrowing costlier.
Q. Credit rating agencies assess the ability of borrowers to repay their debts.
R. That is why governments and companies guard their ratings closely.
S. A high rating lets a borrower raise funds at a lower interest rate.
explanation: Definition, benefit, contrast, conclusion.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To bite the bullet.
options: To face an unpleasant situation with courage
explanation: It means enduring something painful stoically.
